messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, HelixAI Procurement <procurement@helix.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity commitment clarification — HelixAI (DL-6789)

Hi team,

Following up from last week's commercial sync — HelixAI has asked for a clearer timeline and vendor coordination plan tied to the DL-6789 commitment. They want to know:

- What exact GPU SKUs we plan to commit to (count + class) and whether OEM deliveries can be scheduled as staggered tranches.
- Whether we can bridge the onramp with cloud reserved instances or short-term bursts while OEM units are in transit.
- If OEM lead times are variable, can we get firm quotes with an ETA band and any optional expedited lanes (and the incremental delta for expedited shipping)?

Attached is the capacity request Helix shared. It has their projected token throughput and target Q4 go-live. For planning, please confirm:

- Ben: can you check with CloudAtlas and our cloud partners on reserved capacity windows and pricing for bursts (esp. GPU family matching L40s / A100-class)?
- Rafael: what procurement timeline do we need to hit to align OEM shipments with Helix's Q4 onboarding? PO by mid-June?
- Marissa: given the timeline risk, recommend a staged onramp (short-term cloud + staggered OEM) and a fallback quantization profile that reduces initial unit count by 25% — can you draft a proposal?

Goal: produce a single one-page plan by EOD next Wednesday that we can share with Helix and include in the SOW.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Strategic Accounts Manager | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
Attachment: HelixAI_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Gonzalo Morales <gonzalo@vertexhw.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Capacity commitment clarification — HelixAI (DL-6789)

Hi Irene / Marissa / Ben,

Thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick response from Vertex on lead time and options:

- L40S-class (32GB equiv): standard lead time 8–12 weeks from PO receipt. Expedited lane (air freight + factory priority) can reduce to 4–6 weeks with a ~22% surcharge on unit price.
- A100-class (40GB): current lead time 16–22 weeks; we have a small Q4 allocation pool but it requires non-refundable deposit and a 30% early-commitment discount.

We can do staggered shipments: partial ship at 50% after first batch ready, remainder follows as units become available. We will provide a formal quote (VH-5542) with options A/B/C (standard, expedited, deposit-linked allocation). Attached is the outline PDF.

Also flagged: CloudAtlas (our listed partner) reports constrained availability of reserved GPU capacity matching A100-class in their us-west regions until mid-Q4. They suggested short-term bursts on L40S-class equivalents for early testing, then migrate to A100-class as OEM deliveries land. We can introduce the CloudAtlas contact if you want capacity-to-contract conversations initiated from your side.

Please let me know the following asap:
- Which SKU(s) you want priced under standard vs expedited?
- Is Helix willing to consider a deposit to secure a Q4 allocation for A100-class?

Best,

Gonzalo Morales
Director, Sales Operations | Vertex Hardware
gonzalo@vertexhw.com
Attachment: VertexHW_quote_VH-5542.pdf (quote stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity commitment clarification — HelixAI (DL-6789)

Thanks Gonzalo — helpful. Quick internal proposal based on the constraints:

Proposal (staged onramp):
- Phase 0 (short-term testing, weeks 1–8): provision 40 L40S-class GPU-equivalents via CloudAtlas bursts/reserved short-term at negotiated rates. Use quantized model variant to match Helix latency/quality targets for early beta.
- Phase 1 (initial production, weeks 9–20): accept OEM staggered delivery — take first tranche of 60 A100-class units (or equivalent) via Vertex expedited lane for earlier production capacity.
- Phase 2 (scale to commit): remaining OEM units delivered by end of Q4 to reach full committed capacity tied to DL-6789.

Operational asks / dependencies:
- Procurement: need PO in hand by 2027-06-15 to hit phased delivery dates (expedited tranche requires signed PO + deposit).
- Cloud: Ben — confirm pricing & test window for L40S-equivalent bursts; we need a firm quote for the SOW.
- Product: Dev — confirm quantization profile that reduces GPU footprint by ~25% without violating Helix SLOs; produce fallback config.

I've drafted a one-page staged onramp plan (attached). If we agree, I'll share this with Helix and ask for a formal acceptance of the phased timeline and deposit terms.

-Marissa
Head of Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: staged_onramp_plan.pdf (plan stub)

Quick update from procurement/cloud side:

1) CloudAtlas: I have a 30-min sync booked with their capacity team tomorrow. Preliminary reads: they can provide L40S-equivalent capacity for an 8–12 week burst at our requested scale; pricing TBD but should be within our bridging budget line. I'll push to get a firm quote and include 2–4 reserved nodes as a soft hold.

2) Vendor coordination: Rafael, I will open the purchase ticket for Vertex (quote VH-5542). Rafael — please review payment terms; Vertex requires either an expedite surcharge or 30% deposit for allocation. If we go deposit route, we get softer lead-time guarantees.

3) Next steps for Helix SOW: Marissa, once you sign off on the staged plan I will attach Vendor quote VH-5542 and the CloudAtlas quote to the SOW. I'll also add a clause for staggered delivery and optional expedited lane pricing.

4) Risk callouts: OEM lead time volatility; cloud partner regional constraints; and potential customs delays for cross-border shipments (if any units ship from EMEA). Recommend we ask Helix to accept a phased acceptance schedule tied to milestone payments.

I'll update the ticket with the CloudAtlas quote and Vertex PO draft once I have them.
